Bug_Details:
Explicitly calling Thread.run() method will execute in the caller's thread of control.  Instead, call Thread.start() for the intended behavior.
Examples:
Thread t = new Thread();
t.run();            // use t.start() instead
new Thread().run(); // same violation
Bug_Explanation: The code explicitly calls the run() method on Thread objects instead of start(). This causes the run method to execute in the caller's thread of control instead of starting a new thread.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug() method, which explicitly calls run() on Thread objects. This triggers the bug because the run() method executes in the caller's thread, which is not the intended behavior.
